name: Slovenia
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Slavic settlement of the eastern Alps
claims.summary: Slavic peoples migrated into the eastern Alpine valleys after the fall of Roman authority, becoming the ancestors of the Slovenes and establishing the linguistic foundation of the later nation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-600-slavic-settlement-of-the-eastern-alps, claim TL:SVN:event:600:slavic-settlement-of-the-eastern-alps, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Carantania
claims.summary: The Slavic principality of Carantania took shape in the eastern Alps, centred north of present-day Slovenia, and is remembered for the enthronement of its dukes in the Slovene language at the Prince's Stone.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-658-founding-of-carantania, claim TL:SVN:event:658:founding-of-carantania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carantania under Frankish overlordship
claims.summary: Allied with Bavaria against the Avars, Carantania was drawn into the Frankish realm and gradually Christianised, ending its independence and binding the region to the Holy Roman Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-745-carantania-under-frankish-overlordship, claim TL:SVN:event:745:carantania-under-frankish-overlordship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carniola first attested
claims.summary: The march of Carniola, in the central part of present-day Slovenia, appears in the records as a frontier zone of the empire, the nucleus of the duchy that would later define the Slovene lands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-973-carniola-first-attested, claim TL:SVN:event:973:carniola-first-attested, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Habsburgs acquire Carniola and Carinthia
claims.summary: Carinthia and Carniola passed to the Habsburg dynasty, which already held Styria, bringing nearly all the Slovene lands under the rule that would last about six centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1335-habsburgs-acquire-carniola-and-carinthia, claim TL:SVN:event:1335:habsburgs-acquire-carniola-and-carinthia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carniola raised to a duchy
claims.summary: Carniola was elevated to the status of a duchy, consolidating the core territorial unit of the Slovene lands, with Ljubljana as its principal city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1364-carniola-raised-to-a-duchy, claim TL:SVN:event:1364:carniola-raised-to-a-duchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First books printed in Slovene
claims.summary: Primoz Trubar published the Catechismus and Abecedarium, the first printed books in the Slovene language, founding the literary language as a product of the Protestant Reformation.

sources.label: Protestantism and the First Slovene Books

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1550-first-books-printed-in-slovene, claim TL:SVN:event:1550:first-books-printed-in-slovene, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dalmatin's Bible and Bohoric's grammar
claims.summary: Jurij Dalmatin published a complete Slovene translation of the Bible and Adam Bohoric the first Slovene grammar, proving the new written language fit for the most demanding texts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1584-dalmatin-s-bible-and-bohoric-s-grammar, claim TL:SVN:event:1584:dalmatin-s-bible-and-bohoric-s-grammar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mercury found at Idrija
claims.summary: Mercury was first discovered at Idrija, which grew into one of the world's two largest mercury mines; the site is today recognised by UNESCO as part of the Heritage of Mercury.

sources.label: Heritage of Mercury. Almaden and Idrija

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1490-mercury-found-at-idrija, claim TL:SVN:event:1490:mercury-found-at-idrija, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Illyrian Provinces
claims.summary: Napoleon organised the southern Slovene lands as the Illyrian Provinces of the French Empire, with Ljubljana as their capital, introducing reforms and giving the Slovene language a place in public life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1809-the-illyrian-provinces, claim TL:SVN:event:1809:the-illyrian-provinces, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Austria regains the Slovene lands
claims.summary: After Napoleon's defeat the Congress of Vienna restored Habsburg rule over the Illyrian territories, returning the Slovene lands to the Austrian Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1815-austria-regains-the-slovene-lands, claim TL:SVN:event:1815:austria-regains-the-slovene-lands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Preseren writes Zdravljica
claims.summary: The poet France Preseren composed Zdravljica, a toast to liberty and the brotherhood of nations whose seventh stanza became the lyric of the Slovene national anthem after independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1844-preseren-writes-zdravljica, claim TL:SVN:event:1844:preseren-writes-zdravljica, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The United Slovenia programme
claims.summary: During the Spring of Nations, Slovene activists demanded a single autonomous unit joining all Slovene districts of the monarchy with the Slovene language in public use, marking the birth of modern Slovene politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1848-the-united-slovenia-programme, claim TL:SVN:event:1848:the-united-slovenia-programme, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of the Yugoslav kingdom
claims.summary: After the brief State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, the Slovene lands joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, proclaimed on 1 December 1918 and renamed the Kingdom of Yugoslavia in 1929.

sources.label: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1918-birth-of-the-yugoslav-kingdom, claim TL:SVN:event:1918:birth-of-the-yugoslav-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Carinthian Plebiscite
claims.summary: In the disputed southern Carinthian basin, a majority of about 59 per cent voted to remain with Austria rather than join Yugoslavia, leaving a Slovene minority on the Austrian side of the border.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1920-the-carinthian-plebiscite, claim TL:SVN:event:1920:the-carinthian-plebiscite, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Rapallo and the Italian border
claims.summary: Under the Treaty of Rapallo, Italy gained the Slovene Littoral, the Karst and parts of Inner Carniola, subjecting a large Slovene population to Italian and later Fascist rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1920-treaty-of-rapallo-and-the-italian-border, claim TL:SVN:event:1920:treaty-of-rapallo-and-the-italian-border, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Axis partition of Slovenia
claims.summary: Following the invasion of Yugoslavia, the Axis powers carved up the Slovene lands among Germany, Italy and Hungary, while a Liberation Front founded in Ljubljana launched armed resistance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1941-axis-partition-of-slovenia, claim TL:SVN:event:1941:axis-partition-of-slovenia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovenia within socialist Yugoslavia
claims.summary: Slovenia became one of the six republics of Tito's Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, developing into its most prosperous and industrialised member.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1945-slovenia-within-socialist-yugoslavia, claim TL:SVN:event:1945:slovenia-within-socialist-yugoslavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: London Memorandum on Trieste
claims.summary: The United States, United Kingdom, Italy and Yugoslavia agreed to divide the Free Territory of Trieste, placing Zone A under Italian and Zone B under Yugoslav administration.

sources.label: The Trieste Settlement, October 1954 (London Memorandum)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (FRUS 1952-54, vol. VIII)

sources.label: Treaty of Osimo (1975) and the Trieste settlement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1954-london-memorandum-on-trieste, claim TL:SVN:event:1954:london-memorandum-on-trieste, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Osimo
claims.summary: Italy and Yugoslavia signed the Treaty of Osimo, making the partition of the former Free Territory of Trieste definitive and settling the long-disputed western border.

sources.label: Treaty of Osimo (1975) and the Trieste settlement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1975-treaty-of-osimo, claim TL:SVN:event:1975:treaty-of-osimo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plebiscite on independence
claims.summary: In a plebiscite with 93.2 per cent turnout, some 88.5 per cent of all eligible Slovene voters chose independence from Yugoslavia, providing the mandate for statehood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1990-plebiscite-on-independence, claim TL:SVN:event:1990:plebiscite-on-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence and the Ten-Day War
claims.summary: Slovenia declared independence on 25 June 1991; the Yugoslav army's intervention sparked the Ten-Day War, which the Slovenes won, leading to the Brioni Declaration of 7 July and the withdrawal of federal forces.

sources.label: Brioni Agreement and the end of the Ten-Day War
sources.publisher: Zentrum fur Osteuropa- und internationale Studien (ZOiS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-1991-independence-and-the-ten-day-war, claim TL:SVN:event:1991:independence-and-the-ten-day-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slovenia joins NATO
claims.summary: After a 2003 referendum approved by some two-thirds of voters, Slovenia became a member of NATO on 29 March 2004, anchoring its security in the Western alliance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-2004-slovenia-joins-nato, claim TL:SVN:event:2004:slovenia-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Slovenia joined the European Union on 1 May 2004 in the bloc's largest enlargement, the only former Yugoslav republic to accede in that wave.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:SVN:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Adoption of the euro
claims.summary: Slovenia became the first of the 2004 entrants to adopt the euro, replacing the tolar on 1 January 2007 and completing its integration into the core of the European Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-2007-adoption-of-the-euro, claim TL:SVN:event:2007:adoption-of-the-euro, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arbitration Agreement with Croatia
claims.summary: Slovenia and Croatia signed an Arbitration Agreement submitting their land and maritime border dispute, including Piran Bay, to the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague.

sources.label: Arbitration between the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Slovenia (PCA Case No. 2012-04, Final Award 29 June 2017)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-2009-arbitration-agreement-with-croatia, claim TL:SVN:event:2009:arbitration-agreement-with-croatia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: PCA award on the Piran Bay border
claims.summary: The Permanent Court of Arbitration rendered its Final Award, fixing the land and maritime boundary through Piran Bay and granting Slovenia a junction to the high seas; Slovenia accepted the award, Croatia rejected it.

sources.label: Arbitration between the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Slovenia (PCA Case No. 2012-04, Final Award 29 June 2017)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Slovenia: From the Slavic principality of Carantania to a European republic on the sunny side of the Alps.", terralore.co/country/SVN/chronicle#ev-2017-pca-award-on-the-piran-bay-border, claim TL:SVN:event:2017:pca-award-on-the-piran-bay-border, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
